name: argument summary makes a profile resolvable
claim: With an argument summary per call, path and command step validators resolve from a turn profile alone (F1: 0 of 59 resolved from profiles that held tool names only), without any turn text or file content in the profile.

models.result: perTurn[].args in the profile; arguments stored by handle keep their summary in message x.args; a reader registered through the validators seam resolves path and command steps from a profile (node check); the built-in profile reader in app/validators.js is unchanged, and the F1 retest has not been re-run on real profiles
models.evidence: app/profile.js argSummary, app/main.js swap site, scripts/test-profile.mjs, scripts/smoke.mjs

models.result: the built-in profile reader now uses perTurn[].args (change made by this model through the harness, commits b7a5c1e f29dacc 8c8bb8d); on that session's own profile 11 of 11 checkable validators resolved (pass 1, fail 10 absent) against 0 of 66 on profiles without summaries; a Spec: commit message inside git commit -m on a shell command line is not seen (pattern anchored at the start of an argument)

retest: 1 turn profile resolved 0 of 11 (no arguments)
retest: 1 turn profile, shared with qwen/qwen3.7-flash, resolved 0 of 11 (no arguments)

retest, narrowed: one live session doing spec-first work with the shell on a host; its profile with argument summaries resolved 11 of 11 checkable validators (pass 1, fail 10 absent, 4 of them Spec: shapes the session met inside shell command lines); no flow attribution yet

name: host shell backend
claim: A session's shell tool can run on a host exec target (WSL user or container) while its name, schema, description and result shape stay byte-identical to the in-browser machine.

models.result: Real bridge on Windows, 2026-11-20, targets wsl: (user wh) and wsl-podman: (container wh-dev, user dev); all 38 checks of the run held (both targets, the limits, and the page). Per call about 0.35 s (wsl) and 1.8 s (container). node --check app/main.js status 0; git status --short status 0; exit 7 with both streams in order; 3 s timeout answered in 3.3 s / 4.7 s with no process left in the distro or the container; dropped request stopped; 1.3 MB whole, 21 MB cut at 4,000,000 and marked; fifth concurrent call refused. From the page: tools and first message byte-identical on both targets; result text the same as the machine's. Limits found: a container whose process 1 does not reap keeps stopped commands' children as defunct entries (start it with --init); the tmux option could not be switched on with the in-page machine off until vmTmux became a Paste config field; with tmux each command is still its own bash (cd and export do not carry), as in the in-page machine. Not measured: a real model, docker, a Linux-run bridge against a container, macOS.

first real model run, 2026-11-20: container target (wsl-podman), 119 shell calls over 125 requests, task completed with 3 commits and the suites green, $0.01206; first request held none of the terms that name the harness or a browser; found: no retry on a provider 502, run_js runs elsewhere than the shell (4 of 5 calls errors), no edit tool for host files, shell results over about 1,500 chars need output_read, the 8-round stop cut the work 14 times

fault: with the shell on a host, tried to reach the file system from run_js (which runs elsewhere); 4 of 5 run_js calls were errors
handled: the error is returned as the tool result; nothing tells the model where run_js runs

fault: HTTP 502 Provider returned error on 2 of 125 requests (OpenRouter route)
handled: not handled: the turn stops as failed with no retry, and wh say / wh step print nothing that names it; the operator sent continue
